0. FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institit-

tion on 11 December 1967, after the draft finalized by the Hospital Equipment Sectional Committee had been approved by the Consumer Products Division Council.

0.2 The formulation of Indian Standards on hospital equipment has been taken up at the instance of Advisory Committee for the Development of Surgical Instruments, Equipment and Appliances, Government of India. 0.3 This standard is one of a series of Indian Stardards on hospital furniture. Other standards in the series are: IS : 4035-1967 Specification for trolleys, stretcher IS : 4036-1967 Specification for trolleys, patient IS : 4037-1967 Specification for stretcher and stretcher carriers IS : 4266- 1967 Specification for lockers, bedside IS : 4267-1967 Specification for stands, wash hand basin IS : 4455-1967 Specification for trolleys, soiled linen 0.4 In preparing this standard, assistance has been derived from B.S. 1895 : 1952 ` Specification for metal-framed wheeled screens for use in hospitals ' published by British Standards Institution. 0.5 In some of the clauses of this standard, reference has been made to IS : 4033* and IS : 4034-t which are under preparation. Until these standards are published, the requirements in such clauses shall be subject to agreement between the concerned parties. 0.6 Suggestions relating Appendix A. to curtains for the screens are given in

*General requirements for hospital furniture ( wtdcr preporation ).
tSpecification for castors for hospital equipment ( under preparation ).

2

0.7 This standard contains a clause 3.1 which calls for agreement betwe& the purchaser and the manufacturer. 0.8 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of thi# standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, express@&, the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-196W. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard specifies the requirements of metal-framed bedside screens used in hospitals and other similar institutions. 2. MATERIAL 2.1 Framework - shall conform to 2.1 of IS : 4033 - 1968 2.2 castors - shall conform to IS : 4034 3. SHAPE AND DIMENSIONS 3.1 The framework of the screen shall comprise 3 or 4 panels as required by the purchaser, each panel being 610 mm wide in case of4-panel screen; the middle panel being 1 220 mm and the two side panels 610 mm wide in case of 3-panel screen. 3.1.1 The tube used for the panels shall have outside diameter 19.05 mm and thickness 0.91 mm. The height of the panels shall be approximately 1 525 mm. The panels shall be mounted on castors attached to tubular supports or extreme vertical tubes as shown in Fig. 1 and 2, giving an overall height of 1 675 mm. 4. MANUFACTURE 4.1 Framework -Each panel of the framework shall consist of two straight tubes and two bends. The framework shall be so constructed that each panel folds flat on its neighbour. For supporting the curtains, each panel shall be fitted with hooks and expanding wires.

F I G. 3 B EDSIDE S CREEN H I N G E , ALTERNATE S H A P E 4.2 Hinges -Each pair of adjacent panels forming a screen shall be connected by two hinges or a continuous hinge. In case two hinges are used, these shall provide the following features: Smooth unrestricted rotation of panels; b) Parallelism, within a tolerance of 2", between the adjacent tubes of the hinged panels; A 4 maximum gap of 3 mm between the adjacent tubes of the hinged panels ( preferably no gap ); and 4 Sufficiently robust construction to minimize the effects of stresses encountered in normal use, such as those imposed by overturning the screen or by wheeling the screen along uneven ground.

a>

6

Is:4458-1967 4.3 Castors -The screen shall be supplied on not less than six castors, 50 mm dia. The castors shall be of swivel type, rubber-tread and shall be so arranged that when the screen is folded, these do not collide and when the screen is open, it is stable. These shall be so constructed as to obviate clogging by the accumulatio of dust and foreign matter. For rest of the details 4.2 of IS : 4033- 196 3 Tzihall apply. 5. FmIsH 5.1 The finish shall conform to 5 of IS : 4033 -1968'*. 6. MARKING 6.1 The marking shall be as specified in 7 of IS : 4033.1968,. 7. PACKING 7.1 The packing shall be as specified in 8 of IS : 4033 -1968*

APPENDIX A ( Clause 0.6 )
CURTAINS FOR BEDSIDE SCREENS A-I. Ko requirements for curtains have been included in this standard as it isconsidered that the choice of material for curtains of the screen should rest with the purchaser. It is, however, desirable that the material should be opaque, light in weight, durable and suitable for frequent laundering.
